it proper. Thus there are at most nine components in total,
or eight if one is not a singleton.

A component with nonplanar triangle completion is not a singleton,
so the latter bound leaves at most four components besides the
chosen twins. Otherwise, Lemma~\ref{lem:flat-replacement} makes
every component a singleton. The graph is then determined by the
numbers of vertices with neighborhoods $\{a,b,c\},\{a,b,d\},\{a,c,d\},\{b,c,d\}$, with
at least two having each of the first two neighborhoods, at most
nine in total, and $cd$ absent or present.
